label: copy phase of length-3 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or on <DEL>), almost all on the shortest sequences: L=3 accounts for 87% of activation mass (rate 16% vs 0.26% base), L=4 for 10%, and longer sequences barely at all. It peaks at recall_idx 2 (the last output of an L=3 sequence, t=5, 67% of mass), then recall_idx 1. Every activation is on a repeated input (in_first=0, i.e. a fed-back copy of an earlier token). Magnitude depends strongly on which token is being re-input: d and w give the largest activations (top examples are all L=3 with d/w/v in position 1), and digits and sequences with many digits suppress it. Within L=3 copy steps it is active on only about half, and which half depends on token identity in a way no simple token set captures. Predicate (L==3)&(phase==2): dev P=0.47, R=0.73, F1=0.58, mass recall 0.87.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: d, w, m, y, k, h; least: p, f, j, z) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: v, h, w, n; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=3 & t=5, L=3 & t=4.
